hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: A new Debug pane (peer *Pane.tsx in app.tsx's switcher, k6) with pane-local inner sub-tab navigation over three sections — Daemon, MCP, Logs — backed by a new debug service added to makeServices. The chosen shape (a1) keeps the daemon surface minimal: the status card reuses the existing daemon.status IPC, and the ONE genuinely new daemon contract (a read-only debug-status IPC that returns the daemon's own list of currently-attached socket clients, backed by per-connection tracking in the socket server) is built and consumed entirely inside the MCP-section story. Everything else is client-side: the POSIX orphan scan/kill keys on the managed daemon entry and OS signals (k3), and the log viewer fs.watch-tails the two rotated files on disk (k4) — so the Daemon and Logs sections keep working when the daemon is unreachable. The only cross-STORY contract is the pane's section-hosting shape + the debug-service facade that every section plugs into; it is owned by the foundational scaffold story (S001) that every section story already depends on.

consumedContracts.name: Debug pane section-hosting shape + DebugService facade

boundary.internal: The fs.watch rotation-aware tailer over the two PATHS.logDir files (daemon.log, agent.log), the most-recent-segment resolution + follow-across-rotation, and the persistent level/module/free-text filter bar. Entirely client-side (k4); consumes only sc1.

api.name: DebugService
api.signature: export interface DebugService { readonly sections: readonly DebugSection[]; daemonStatus(): Promise<DaemonCardModel>; scanOrphans(): OrphanScanResult; killOrphans(pids: readonly number[]): Promise<KillOutcome[]>; attachedClients(): Promise<DebugStatusModel>; mcpStatus(): Promise<readonly McpClientStatus[]>; logCategories(): readonly LogCategory[]; tailLog(categoryId: LogCategoryId, onLines: (lines: readonly LogLine[]) => void): () => void }

returns.meaning: The sc1 facade gains two additive members for the Logs section: logCategories() (the static daemon + agent categories, ac1) and tailLog(categoryId, onLines) (start a rotation-aware fs.watch tail of that category's active segment, returning a dispose(); ac2/lc2). Existing members unchanged. Same flat extension model as s2/s3/s4.

postconditions: Additive to sc1 — existing members unchanged; s1-s4 fakes stubbing `debug` must add logCategories + tailLog stubs.

api.name: logCategories

returns.meaning: The fixed set of log categories the pane can tail: { id:'daemon'; title:'Daemon'; stem:'daemon' } and { id:'agent'; title:'Agent'; stem:'agent' } — derived from PATHS.logDir + the pino-roll stems (daemon.log → daemon.*.log, agent.log → agent.*.log). Synchronous, static — listing does NOT start any stream (ac1).

postconditions: Exactly two categories (daemon, agent); no stream is opened by calling this.

api.name: tailLog
api.signature: tailLog(categoryId: LogCategoryId, onLines: (lines: readonly LogLine[]) => void): () => void

parameters.name: categoryId
parameters.purpose: Which category to follow. Selecting a different category is done by disposing the prior subscription and calling tailLog again (only one active stream, ac2).

parameters.name: onLines
parameters.purpose: Sink for parsed lines: called once with the active segment's last-N lines on start, then again with each new batch of appended lines (and the new segment's lines after a rotation).

returns.meaning: A dispose() that stops the fs.watch (+ any pending re-resolve) and guarantees onLines is never called again. Idempotent. The core is tailLogWith(deps) over an injectable fs seam so rotation/append/parse are unit-testable without a real watcher.

errors.condition: A missing log dir / no matching segment / a read or watch error resolves to an empty initial emit + a quiet retry on the next fs event; the tailer never throws to the caller (the section keeps working even with no logs yet, k4).

preconditions: Read-only — opens the rotated log files for reading only; never writes, never touches the daemon (k4/k2).
onLines is invoked only between start and dispose().
postconditions: On start, emits the active (highest-N / newest-mtime) segment's last-N lines; thereafter emits appended lines live and follows across a rotation to a newer segment (lc2).
After dispose(), no further onLines call and no lingering watcher.

api.name: LogsSection
api.signature: export function LogsSection(props: { services: { readonly debug: DebugService } }): ReactElement

parameters.name: props
parameters.purpose: Supplies the debug facade whose logCategories()/tailLog() the section drives.

returns.meaning: The Logs section component (replaces the s1 'Log viewer — coming soon.' placeholder in DebugPane's SECTION_VIEWS). Lists the categories (ac1); on select, subscribes via tailLog into a bounded ring buffer (disposing any prior subscription so only one streams, ac2) with the subscription torn down on unmount/section-change; renders (via the LogView widget) the buffer filtered by a persistent { level?; module?; text? } filter bar applied as a pure predicate (ac3). The free-text filter entry uses the capture gate; the section is strictly read-only (k2).

preconditions: Rendered by DebugPane only when the logs section is active.
postconditions: No mutating control (k2); the active tail subscription is disposed on unmount / category change (no watcher leak).

api.name: LogLine
api.signature: export interface LogLine { readonly raw: string; readonly time?: number; readonly level?: number; readonly module?: string; readonly msg?: string }

returns.meaning: One parsed tail line. `raw` is always the verbatim line (free-text filter matches it); time/level/module/msg are the best-effort pino-JSON fields (level = numeric pino level, module = pino `name`). A non-JSON / partial line keeps only `raw` so level/module filters skip it while free-text still matches (graceful degrade).

api.name: LogCategory
api.signature: export interface LogCategory { readonly id: LogCategoryId; readonly title: string; readonly stem: string }; export type LogCategoryId = 'daemon' | 'agent'

returns.meaning: A tailable log category: `id` (the closed union daemon|agent), `title` (display), `stem` (the pino-roll file stem used to glob `<stem>.*.log` in PATHS.logDir). Structured data only.

api.name: LogFilter
api.signature: export interface LogFilter { readonly minLevel?: number; readonly module?: string; readonly text?: string }

returns.meaning: The persistent filter bar state applied as a pure predicate over the ring buffer: minLevel (keep LogLines whose numeric level >= minLevel; non-JSON lines with no level are dropped by an active level filter), module (case-insensitive match on LogLine.module), text (case-insensitive substring over LogLine.raw). An unset field imposes no constraint. CLI-side view state — not persisted to disk.

errorCases.scenario: The log directory does not exist yet, or a selected category has no matching segment (no logs written yet).
errorCases.detection: listSegments(stem) returns an empty array (readdir on a missing dir throws ENOENT, caught inside the seam / core; a present dir with no `<stem>.*.log` yields []).
errorCases.response: tailLog emits an empty initial batch and installs a directory-level retry (re-resolve on the next fs event) rather than throwing; the section renders an empty tail with the category still selected.
errorCases.userImpact: The operator sees the category selected with no lines (not a crash); once the daemon/agent writes its first segment, lines begin streaming.

errorCases.scenario: The active segment is read or watched and the fs call throws (permission denied, file removed mid-read by rotation cleanup, watcher error event).
errorCases.detection: readTail/watch in the fs seam throws or the fs.watch emits an 'error'; the tailLogWith core catches around each fs interaction.
errorCases.response: Swallow the individual failure, keep the subscription alive, and re-resolve the active segment on the next event (so a file deleted by rotation cleanup is replaced by the newer segment). Never rethrow to onLines.
errorCases.userImpact: A transient fs hiccup shows as a brief pause in streaming, not a crash; streaming resumes on the next write/rotation.

errorCases.scenario: onLines fires after the operator switched category or unmounted the section (an in-flight fs event races the dispose()).
errorCases.detection: The dispose() sets a `disposed` flag the core checks before every onLines call (and removes the fs watcher).
errorCases.response: A post-dispose emit is suppressed by the flag; the watcher is already removed. Only the current subscription's lines ever reach the section (single-stream, ac2).
errorCases.userImpact: Switching categories never bleeds stale lines from the previous stream into the new one; no post-unmount setState.

errorCases.scenario: A tail line is not valid pino JSON (a pretty-printed line, a partial trailing line written mid-flush, or a truncated head after tailing into the middle of a line).
errorCases.detection: JSON.parse of the line throws inside the per-line parser.
errorCases.response: Fall back to a LogLine carrying only `raw` (no level/module/msg). Free-text filter still matches `raw`; an active level/module filter treats it as non-matching (dropped) rather than crashing.
errorCases.userImpact: Non-JSON lines remain visible under no/text filters and are simply not surfaced under a level/module filter — no parse crash, no silently-swallowed content.

edgeCases.input: The Logs section is opened but no category is selected yet.
edgeCases.expected: The category list (daemon, agent) renders and NO stream is started (ac1) — no fs.watch is installed until a selection.

edgeCases.input: The operator switches from category A to category B while A is streaming.
edgeCases.expected: A's subscription is disposed (watcher removed) before B's tailLog starts; only B streams (ac2). The ring buffer resets to B's tail.

edgeCases.input: The active segment rolls over to a new higher-N segment while streaming (a daily/size rotation).
edgeCases.expected: The tailer detects the active file stopped growing AND a newer segment appeared, re-resolves to it, and continues emitting the new segment's lines — the operator keeps seeing new lines with no gap/action (lc2).

edgeCases.input: A level/module/text filter is set, then cleared, while the stream continues.
edgeCases.expected: Setting a filter immediately limits the VISIBLE lines to matches (the stream keeps accumulating underneath); clearing it re-reveals the buffered lines — filtering is a pure re-render over the ring buffer, never a re-read (ac3).

edgeCases.input: The ring buffer reaches its bound while streaming a busy log.
edgeCases.expected: The oldest lines scroll off (bounded last-N, like LogView) so memory stays bounded; the newest lines and the active filter view are always current.

edgeCases.input: The operator presses a key looking for a way to delete/rotate/clear the log.
edgeCases.expected: No key mutates or clears any log file; only category-select + filter entry + the pane's section-nav are honoured. The section is strictly read-only (k2).

invariantsToPreserve.text: The Logs section reads log data DIRECTLY from disk via fs.watch over the known rotated files (PATHS.logDir daemon.*.log / agent.*.log) with NO new daemon log-streaming IPC, so it functions even when the daemon is unreachable (k4). This is an event-driven watch, not a poll loop, per the HLD nonFunctional.

Streaming follows the currently-active (highest-N / newest-mtime) rotated segment and continues across a rotation by re-resolving to the newer segment (lc2), so new lines keep appearing after the underlying file rolls over. The pino-roll segment naming is `<stem>.<N>.<ext>` (verified against the live /tmp/.insrc).

The Debug pane is read-only apart from the single s3 orphan-kill action (k2): the Logs section only reads/watches files for display + applies in-memory filters; it never writes, deletes, rotates, or clears a log, and never touches the daemon. It reuses the existing LogView widget for rendering.

migration.backwardCompat: The only touched surface is the sc1 DebugService facade, extended with two ADDITIVE members (logCategories + tailLog) — every existing member and every existing debug caller is unchanged; the in-repo fakes gain conformant stubs in the same change so the whole CLI suite still compiles. No cross-process/wire type is touched (unlike s4): the tailer is entirely client-side and reads only from disk, so there is no CLI↔daemon compatibility surface. No public API signature is removed or renamed. Rolling back is deleting the two facade members + LogsSection and restoring the logs placeholder; nothing persists.

alternativesConsidered.name: Subscription tailer (onLines callback + dispose) with a client-side filter over a ring buffer
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The facade exposes logCategories() + a tailLog(category, onLines) that reads the active segment's tail, fs.watch-follows appends + rotation (lc2), and returns a dispose(); the LogsSection applies level/module/text filters as a pure predicate over an accumulated ring buffer.

alternativesConsidered.name: Async-iterable / EventEmitter tail stream
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: tailLog(category) returns an AsyncIterable<LogLine[]> (or an EventEmitter) the component drains; filtering still client-side.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Functionally equivalent to a1 but the for-await/EventEmitter teardown is harder to cancel cleanly in a React effect (AbortController + break, listener-leak risk) than a1's plain dispose() — more failure surface for no gain in a single-consumer UI stream.

alternativesConsidered.name: Snapshot-poll tail (readLogTail(category, offset) polled by the component)
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: No fs.watch — the facade exposes readLogTail(category, sinceOffset) -> { lines, offset } and the component polls it on an interval.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: VIOLATES k4 (the HLD explicitly says the log tail is fs.watch event-driven, NOT a poll loop) — a steady interval re-reads the file even when idle — and only partially meets ac2 (poll latency + fragile offset-across-rotation bookkeeping). Disqualified on the load-bearing invariant.
